guideTitle: 6 Best Non Slip Shower Mats Under $25 in 2026
metaTitle: Best Non Slip Shower Mats Under $25 (2026)
metaDescription: Six budget non slip shower and tub mats compared on suction count, size, drainage and cleaning, so you can pick a grippy mat without overspending.
mainKeyword: best non slip shower mats under 25
introParagraphs: A shower mat is one of the cheapest safety upgrades in a bathroom, and also one of the easiest to get wrong. At a budget level the differences are not about brand prestige. They come down to how many suction cups hold the mat to the floor, whether the mat is cut to fit a tub or a square stall, and whether water and soap can drain through instead of pooling under your feet.

The six picks here span a real spread. The Gorilla Grip 35x16 and the TEESHLY 40x16 cover a full tub floor, the Gorilla Grip 21x21 is cut for a stand-up stall, and the OTHWAY leads on drainage with 360 holes. The BEMISO is the smallest tub mat at 27.5 x 15.7 inches, and the Hargiis trades suction for a thick foam-like surface.

We evaluated each mat from its listing specs and buyer feedback patterns, not from hands-on lab work. Keep in mind that a mat is a grip aid for wet floors, not a grab bar, so it should never be leaned on for balance.

products.name: GORILLA GRIP Bath Tub Shower Mat 35x16
products.description:
The Gorilla Grip 35x16 is the pick that most buyers should start with. It uses a patented layout of hundreds of suction cups underneath and a hexagon pattern with a pebble-textured top, so the grip is delivered by both the underside and the surface your feet meet. The material is listed as BPA-free, and the clear finish lets the tub floor show through, which many people prefer to a colored slab.

The tradeoff is length. At 35 inches it is shorter than the 40-inch TEESHLY, so in a long tub there will be bare floor at one end. Suction mats also only bond to smooth, non-textured tub surfaces, and a Gorilla Grip will not stay put on a floor with a built-in anti-slip pattern. If your tub has that kind of molded texture, none of the suction picks in this list are a good match.

Ownership is simple. Hundreds of drainage holes let water run toward the drain, and the listing says it can go in a washing machine, which beats scrubbing by hand. Compared with the OTHWAY and its 360 drain holes it is a little less drain-focused, but the established design and square-ish proportions make it the safer default. It also sits above most of the others here in cost, so it is the pick for people willing to spend a little more at this budget.
products.bestFor: Standard tubs where you want a proven, washable, full-floor mat.
pros: Hundreds of suction cups plus textured top
Clear BPA-free material shows the tub
Drain holes help water move to the drain
cons: Needs a smooth, untextured tub floor
Costs more than the cheapest mats

products.name: OTHWAY Bathtub Shower Mat Non Slip
products.description:
OTHWAY puts its numbers up front: 198 suction cups and 360 angled drain holes, which the listing contrasts with roughly 250 holes on typical mats. That makes it the drainage leader of this group. Water and soapy runoff pass through quickly, so the surface should be drier under your heel and the mat should be less likely to hold a film of soap against the tub.

The material is a flexible TPE with raised nodules, which gives a mild foot-massage feel and a softer bend than stiff PVC. The flexibility helps it follow a slightly curved tub floor. The downside is that very soft mats can curl at the edges if they are not fully pressed down, so press each cup flat during installation and recheck after the first few showers.

Compared with the Gorilla Grip 35x16, the OTHWAY has fewer stated suction cups than the home-brand claim of hundreds, but its drainage design is the more aggressive of the two. It sits in the cheaper half of the price range, which makes it a sensible choice if standing water is your main complaint. For a household that showers daily, the faster drying is the practical reason to choose it.
products.bestFor: People whose mats stay wet or grow film because of slow drainage.
pros: 198 suction cups hold on smooth floors
Raised nodules add gentle foot massage
cons: Soft edges can curl if not pressed flat
Not for textured or non-smooth tub floors

products.name: TEESHLY 40 x 16 Inch Extra Large Bathtub Mat
products.description:
The TEESHLY is the longest mat in this lineup at 40 x 16 inches, which makes it the best answer for a long standard tub where a 35-inch mat leaves a gap. The surface is a domed, pebble-like pattern in soft-touch PVC, and the listing highlights a massage-like feel under the feet during a shower.

Coverage is its main argument, and that matters more than it sounds. A mat that reaches both the faucet end and the drain end means you are always stepping onto grip rather than bare enamel, especially when you shift position to rinse. The cost is size, since a 40-inch mat is harder to rinse in a small sink and will not suit a compact shower stall.

The listing also describes the mat as machine washable and drained, so routine cleaning is not a chore. Next to the Gorilla Grip 35x16, the TEESHLY adds five inches of length and calls out a soft-touch PVC feel. Pick it for length and a softer hand, and skip it if your tub is short or has a textured floor.
products.bestFor: Long tubs where you want the grip to run the full floor.
cons: Too long for small stalls and short tubs
Large mats are awkward to rinse by hand

products.name: GORILLA GRIP Square Shower Stall Mat 21x21
products.description:
Most shower mats are cut as long rectangles for tubs, which is the wrong shape for a stand-up shower. The Gorilla Grip Square is 21 x 21 inches and sized for a stall floor, where you mainly stand in one spot rather than step across a long basin. It shares the brand's patented suction cup layout and hexagon pebble top.

The square shape is its strength and its limit. It covers where your feet land in a normal shower, but it will not span a wide stall, so a larger walk-in with a linear drain may need two mats or a different product. Check that your stall floor is flat and smooth, because suction cups need a clean bonding surface, and a seam or ridge under the mat will break the seal.

Cleaning is straightforward, since the drain holes let water pass and the BPA-free material is easy to wipe or rinse. It is the second most expensive pick here by rank, so you are paying a little for the shape rather than for extra grip. If you have a tub, take the Gorilla Grip 35x16 instead. If your shower is a stall, this is the pick that actually fits.
products.bestFor: Square or stall-style shower floors that need a compact mat.
pros: Hundreds of suction cups per the listing
Drain holes pass water to the drain
cons: Too small for wide or linear-drain stalls
A seam or ridge can break the suction seal

products.name: BEMISO Shower Mat Non Slip Bathtub Mat 27.5 x 15.7
products.description:
The BEMISO is the smallest rectangle in the roundup, at 27.5 x 15.7 inches, and it relies on more than 160 suction cups plus slotted drain panels. The listing describes TPE and PP construction and positions it as a gentle-touch mat for people with sensitive skin or for use around kids and older adults.

Smaller means easier handling. It is lighter to rinse, dries faster and fits a narrow tub or a shower stall where a 35-inch mat would overhang. The compromise is that it leaves more floor exposed, so it suits people who mostly stand in one place. With fewer suction cups than the OTHWAY at 198, its hold depends on a clean, smooth floor and a firm press during setup.

It lands in the middle of the cost range, which makes it a reasonable compromise for small spaces. If your tub is long and you want full coverage, the TEESHLY is the better fit. If space is tight and you value quick drying, the BEMISO is a clear, simple choice.
products.bestFor: Narrow tubs and small stalls where bigger mats overhang.
pros: Slotted panels drain soapy water fast
cons: Leaves more bare floor in a full-size tub
Fewer suction cups than the OTHWAY

products.name: Hargiis Non Slip Bathtub Mat
products.description:
The Hargiis takes a different approach from the suction-heavy picks. It is 0.4 inch thick with a loofah-like textured top and a plaid backing on the underside, and the listing frames it as a foot comfort and scrubbing mat that also resists slipping. The thickness gives a cushioned feel that stiff, thin mats do not.

The tradeoff is grip method. A plaid backing relies on friction and surface contact rather than a dense grid of suction cups, so it can behave differently on different tub finishes. It is worth testing the first shower with care and pressing it flat. A thicker mat also holds more water, so let it dry fully between uses to avoid mildew.

It sits in the lower middle of the price ladder. Next to the Gorilla Grip 35x16 it gives up the proven suction layout in exchange for a plusher feel. Choose it when comfort under the feet matters to you, and choose a suction-cup pick instead if you want the strongest hold on a slick tub.
products.bestFor: Bathers who want a cushioned, scrubbing surface underfoot.
pros: Loofah-like texture doubles as a scrubber
cons: Backing grips differently from suction cups
Thicker body holds more water until dry

buyingCriteria.explanation: Suction is the main thing holding a mat to a wet floor, so the count and spread of cups matters more than the logo. The OTHWAY lists 198 cups and the BEMISO lists more than 160, while the Gorilla Grip mats state hundreds without a fixed number. Look for cups spread evenly to the corners, because a mat that lifts at one edge will slide. Press every cup down on a warm, clean tub and lift a corner to check the seal before you trust it.

A mat that does not match your floor shape will either overhang or leave bare patches. The TEESHLY at 40 x 16 inches suits long tubs, the Gorilla Grip 35x16 fits a typical tub, the BEMISO at 27.5 x 15.7 suits narrow tubs, and the Gorilla Grip Square at 21 x 21 is for stalls. Measure the flat part of your floor, not the rim to rim width, since the sloped sides do not take suction. Aim for a mat that covers where you actually stand and turn.

Standing water under a mat grows mildew and lets soap film build up, which reduces grip over time. The OTHWAY has 360 drain holes and the BEMISO uses slotted panels, while the Gorilla Grip mats rely on hundreds of holes. More open area usually means faster drying but a slightly less solid surface. Lift the mat weekly and rinse the underside, whatever the drainage design.

Budget mats come in TPE, PVC and PP blends, and each feels different. The OTHWAY and BEMISO use flexible TPE, the TEESHLY uses soft-touch PVC, and the Hargiis uses BPA-free PVC at 0.4 inch thick. Softer materials bend to a curved floor but may curl at the edges, while stiffer ones lie flat but feel harder underfoot. If anyone with sensitive skin uses the shower, check that the listing mentions BPA-free or odorless material.

A mat that cannot be cleaned will become a hygiene problem within weeks. The Gorilla Grip and TEESHLY listings state machine washable use, which makes a monthly wash easy. Mats with deep textures, such as the Hargiis with its scrubber surface, need a rinse after every shower to avoid trapped residue. Hang the mat or stand it up to dry rather than leaving it flat in the tub.

A shower mat reduces slipping on a wet floor, but it is not a balance aid and will not hold your weight. None of these six, from the Gorilla Grip 35x16 to the Hargiis, replace a mounted grab bar for support while standing or stepping over a tub wall. If getting in and out feels unsteady, pair the mat with a properly installed bar or a shower chair. Suction mats also fail on textured or damaged tub finishes, so check your floor first.

howWeEvaluated.title: Grip mechanism
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared how each listing says the mat stays put: counted suction cups on the OTHWAY and BEMISO, patented cup layouts on the two Gorilla Grip mats, and the plaid backing on the Hargiis. The mats with stated cup numbers and an even spread scored highest. Mats relying on a single material feature scored lower.

howWeEvaluated.title: Floor coverage and fit
howWeEvaluated.description: Each mat was judged against common tub and stall dimensions, from the 40 x 16 inch TEESHLY down to the 21 x 21 inch Gorilla Grip Square. A good fit means full coverage of the standing area without overhanging the sloped tub walls. We noted which shapes suit tubs and which suit stalls.

howWeEvaluated.title: Drainage and drying
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at drain hole counts and panel designs, with the OTHWAY leading on 360 holes and the BEMISO using slotted panels. Faster water movement means less soap film and less mildew risk. Thicker textured mats such as the Hargiis were marked down slightly for slower drying.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning and upkeep
howWeEvaluated.description: Listings that mention machine washing, including the Gorilla Grip and TEESHLY, earned more credit than those that rely on rinsing alone. We also considered how easily soap residue can be removed from deeper surface textures.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value at this budget
howWeEvaluated.description: Every mat is within the cap, so we ranked relative value: the Gorilla Grip 35x16 as the strongest all-rounder, the OTHWAY for drainage, the TEESHLY for coverage, and the BEMISO and Hargiis as compact and comfort-focused options. Spending more at this level mainly buys proven design and washability.

howToChoose.intro: Two mechanisms keep a mat in place, and they behave differently.

cards.label: Suction cups
cards.text: Cups create a vacuum seal against smooth enamel or fiberglass and give the firmest hold. The OTHWAY (198 cups), BEMISO (160+), TEESHLY, and both Gorilla Grip mats use this approach. The weakness is textured floors, where the seal fails. Pick this side for most smooth tubs.

cards.label: Friction backing
cards.text: The Hargiis uses a plaid backing that grips by contact and weight rather than vacuum. It tends to suit people who want more cushion and are comfortable testing the hold. Choose it only if comfort matters more than the strongest possible anchor, and press it flat each use.

faq.q: How do I choose between a tub mat and a stall mat?
faq.a: Measure the flat floor area, not the full tub width, then match the shape. Long rectangles like the TEESHLY 40 x 16 and Gorilla Grip 35x16 suit tubs, while the 21 x 21 Gorilla Grip Square suits stalls. A mat that overhangs the sloped wall will not seat well. When in doubt, choose slightly smaller so the cups sit fully on the flat part.

faq.q: Can a good mat replace a grab bar?
faq.a: No. A shower mat improves traction on a wet floor, but it does nothing to help you balance or support your weight. If stepping over a tub wall feels unsteady, add a properly mounted grab bar into studs or rated anchors. Use the mat as the base layer and the bar as the support.

faq.q: How often should I clean a shower mat?
faq.a: Rinse it after every shower and wash it weekly if it traps soap or hair. The Gorilla Grip and TEESHLY listings state machine washable use, which makes this easy. Deeper textures like the Hargiis scrubber surface hold more residue, so flip and rinse the underside. Dry the mat standing up when you can.

faq.q: Why does my suction mat keep sliding?
faq.a: The usual cause is a dirty or textured tub floor, which stops the cups from sealing. Clean the tub, wet the mat, and press every cup down firmly, then lift a corner to test. If your tub has a molded anti-slip pattern, suction mats like the OTHWAY or BEMISO will struggle. In that case a friction backing or a different product is the better route.

faq.q: Is it worth paying more at this budget?
faq.a: A little extra buys polish: clearer materials, established suction designs, and machine-washable use, as with the Gorilla Grip 35x16. The cheaper OTHWAY still gives 198 cups and 360 drain holes. Spend more only if you value the proven design, and save if you simply need a dependable mat.

faq.q: How long do budget shower mats last?
faq.a: Expect to replace a mat when the cups lose grip, the edges curl or mildew stains will not wash out. Frequent drying and washing extends life. Softer TPE mats such as the OTHWAY can wear at the edges sooner than stiffer PVC, so inspect them every few months.
